title: apply names the eval row each rejected fix broke and tries a fact-keyed expansion before an alias
goal: For an eval finding, ql_apply tries its candidates in the order: expansion rows whose fact shares the most question words, then an alias, and records in the finding's observed, per rejected candidate, the one gate that failed with the eval row id or the pack-size figure, so a no-fix finding says which existing row each candidate would have broken; the three no-fix findings of 2026-10-08 that observed names with 'eval fails: EV-...' are replayed on the committed store with --store and the report lists, per finding, each candidate and its breaking row. No alias or expansion that a held-out question of kb/public/_retrieval/lookup_heldout.csv would turn from answered to missed is accepted: the held-out file's answer rate before and after the replay is the story's premise probe.
links: kb/_self/doc2query.md (expansion rows and the Doc2Query-- filter the gates stand in for)
notes: Premise (2026-10-08, main 6be3dcd0): eval findings in state no-fix: 5; three carry observed.gate of one failing eval row each: public/gitlab/automated-merge-requests.md ('eval fails: EV-catch-regression-that-only-slow-full'), public/claude/hooks.md ('eval fails: EV-logs-kb-tooling-keep-query-log'), public/claude/ci-and-headless.md ('eval fails: EV-claude-p-headless-mode-edit-files'); the other two are notes from BG-bbfdisfu. Today apply records the failed gates but not which candidate failed on which row. This story names a quality of answers (which fixes are accepted), so by the plan rule its premise is a held-out probe: it depends on ST-fzvj57al (the held-out file), and the candidate order is changed only if the replay shows the held-out rate does not fall. P3 and outside the first sprints for that reason.
